title: Mid-Day Update: Wall Street Braces For More Trade Restrictions Against China - Nasdaq.com
text:
Mid-Day Update: Wall Street Braces For More Trade Restrictions Against China September 17, 2018, 01:05:05 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo
Plagued by Washington's threats to impose more trade restrictions on Chinese imports and fresh risk aversion in the technology sector, Wall Street's major market averages started the week in the red on Monday. The Dow is orbiting the flat line thanks to gains in the industrial sector, but both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq are taking on more significant losses with consumer discretionary and technology stocks bearing the brunt of selling pressure.
Selling erupted mid-morning as investors braced for an escalation in the trade war between the US and China following a Wall Street Journal report, which claims President Donald Trump is ready to pull the trigger on another $200 billion in tariffs. Losses were heaviest in FAANG and cyclical consumer stocks as investors pivoted into defensive sectors.
Economic data also contributed to the poor price action Monday after the Empire State manufacturing index fell to 19.0 in September, its lowest level in five months and below the estimated 23.0.
The defensive tone across Wall Street was exacerbated by selling pressure on the technology sector, led by Amazon ( AMZN ) and Apple ( AAPL ) following reports of an internal investigation into data leaks by employees, and sluggish sales of the iPhone XS and Max, respectively.
Europe's markets surrendered early gains, led by the export-heavy German DAX with most regional bourses ending the day negative. Buoyed by gains in Bayer and France's Societe Generale, the joint European index closed fractionally higher.
Crude oil was down $0.22 to $68.85 per barrel. Natural gas was up $0.05 to $2.82 per 1 million BTU. Gold was up $6.40 to $1,207.40 an ounce, while silver was up $0.11 to $14.25 an ounce. Copper was up $0.005 to $2.65 per pound.
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund was down 0.28% to $14.46 with the United States Natural Gas Fund up 1.32% to $22.99. Among precious-metal funds, the Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF was up 1.93% to $18.32 while SPDR Gold Shares were up 0.70% to $113.81. The iShares Silver Trust was up 1.04% to $13.37.
